newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crude firms amid thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crude firms amid thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes followed West Texas Intermediate (WTI) higher on Friday amid a thin pre-weekend market, traders said.
No light crude cargoes were traded early Friday and activity on next week's market would turn quiet, traders said, with players attending an annual refinery conference in Texas.

A major West Coast refiner sold Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude to another refiner at -$0.91 cents under April West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Thursday. The shipment, confirmed by both sides, widened the discount 11 cents to $-0.91 cents.
No deals were heard done in heavy crudes or light Line 63 grades.
ANS crude ranged $20.14/20.34 a barrel, up 50 cents in line with WTI, which rose on fund buying and a brief shutdown of London's oil futures market.
Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.
Kern River, a representative heavy grade, stood $14.25/14.35 a barrel, unchanged from Wednesday.
